items.title: R--Purdue Advanced Reactor Core Simulator Code
items.desc:
The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing a presolicitation notice for a requirement entitled, “Technical Support for the Purdue Advanced Reactor Core Simulator (PARCS) Code Suite”

The objective of this acquisition is to obtain regulatory technical support for the maintenance, code support, assessment, continued development, and user training of the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS code suite, including the interfaces between PARCS and RELAP, TRACE, and SNAP. These activities ensure that the PARCS code suite remains a reliable and modern tool for confirmatory reactor physics and systems analysis.

PARCS supports independent regulatory decision making by enabling NRC staff to perform confirmatory evaluations of operator actions, core designs, power uprates, advanced reactor concepts, and license amendment requests. Maintaining and advancing the PARCS/PATHS and GenPMAXS capability is essential for enabling high quality staff reviews under 10 CFR Parts 50 and 52.

At a high level, this acquisition will:

items.desc:
The Town of Whitakers is requesting qualifications from qualified architectural/engineering firms to provide professional services for the proposed Whitakers Community Center project.

The project involves evaluating the Town Hall building for renovation and potential conversion into a Community Center while continuing to accommodate current administrative services. The selected firm may be responsible for site and facility evaluation, geotechnical evaluation if necessary, preparation of a preliminary architectural/engineering report, environmental report if required, assistance with USDA Rural Development funding requirements and application documentation, design services, bidding and construction contract negotiations, and construction administration.

The project is anticipated to be funded through a USDA Rural Development program. The tentative projected funding amount is $1,015,000, inclusive of all soft and hard costs.

The Town will utilize a qualification-based selection process pursuant to North Carolina General Statute 143-64.31 and applicable USDA Rural Development procurement guidelines. Fee proposals will not be considered during the initial qualification-based selection process.

Interested firms shall submit fifteen (15) hard copies of their qualifications package, limited to thirty (30) pages, in accordance with the Request for Qualifications document.
